name: Alaska Ballot Measure 3 (Citizenship Voting)
title: Alaska Citizenship Voting Requirement Initiative
description: Require that only United States citizens may be qualified voters in Alaska elections.

name: Alaska Ballot Measure 2 (Ranked Choice Voting)
title: nonpartisan blanket primaries, and campaign disclosure rules
description: Repeal Alaska Measure 2, eliminating the top-four primaries and ranked-choice voting general elections in Alaska, alongside the established campaign finance provisions requiring persons and entities contributing more than $2,000 derived from donations, contributions, dues, or gifts to disclose the true sources (as defined in law) of their political contributions.

name: Alaska Supreme Court Justice Jude Pate Retention
Alabama Amendment 1 - Fill Lieutenant Governor Vacancies by Election
title: Alabama Require Lieutenant Governor Vacancies to be Filled by Election Amendment
description: Amend the Alabama Constitution to require the office of lieutenant governor to be filled by election if a vacancy occurs more than 60 days before the next general election.

name: Alabama Amendment 2 - School District Consolidation Process
title: Alabama School District Consolidation Process Amendment
description: Amend the Alabama Constitution to establish a process for two or more public county school boards to combine into a single multi-county board of education.

name: Alabama Amendment 4 - Star-Spangled Banner in Public Schools
title: Alabama Broadcast The Star-Spangled Banner in Public Schools Amendment
description: Amend the Alabama Constitution to require all public schools to broadcast or arrange for the performance of the first stanza of The Star-Spangled Banner at least once per week.

name: Alabama Amendment 3 - Pledge of Allegiance and Student-Led Prayer in Public Schools
title: Alabama Require Pledge of Allegiance and Allow Student-Led Prayer in Public Schools Amendment
description: Amend the Alabama Constitution to require public schools to recite the Pledge of Allegiance each day and to allow for student-led prayer.

name: Arkansas Right to Keep and Bear Arms Amendment
title: Arkansas Right to Keep and Bear Arms Amendment
description: Expand the constitutional right to keep and bear arms to include for lawful hunting and recreational use or other lawful purposes, without limitation on the possession and use of ammunition, firearm accessories, or firearm components stating that the right to keep and bear arms is "a natural, fundamental, and individual right that shall not be infringed".

name: Arkansas Creation of Economic Development Districts Amendment
title: Arkansas Authorize Legislature to Create Programs for Economic Development Including Economic Development Districts Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to allow the legislature to create programs, including Economic Development Districts, and make loans and grants of public money to achieve the purposes of unemployment prevention, real estate improvement, and economic, transportation, commerce, and real estate development.

name: Arkansas Citizenship Requirement for Voting Amendment
title: Arkansas Citizenship Requirement for Voting Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to mandate that only U.S. citizens may vote in state or local elections.

name: Arkansas Natural Resources Commission Bond Measure
title: Arkansas Natural Resources Commission Bond Measure
description: Authorize the Arkansas Natural Resources Commission to issue up to $500 million in general obligation bonds to fund water-related infrastructure projects including water treatment and transportation, waste disposal, pollution abatement, drainage, irrigation, flood control, and wetlands and aquatic resources infrastructure.

name: California Supreme Court Associate Justice Seat 6 - Joshua Groban Retention
California Proposition 42
title: California Prohibit New Taxes on Retirement Holdings, Personal Assets, and Savings and Limit Retroactive Taxes Initiative
description: Prohibit the enactment of new taxes after January 1, 2026, on ownership or control of retirement holdings, individually-owned assets, and other forms of personal savings, and retroactive taxes that result in a tax liability based on conduct, activities, or a status that occurred or were present prior to the effective date of the tax.

name: California Proposition 37
title: California Second Mortgage Homebuyer Program and Revenue Bond Initiative
description: Establish a second mortgage homebuyer program for qualified homebuyers on qualifying homes administered by the California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA), and authorize the CalHFA to issue up to $25 billion in bonds to fund the program. The second mortgages would cover up to 17% of the home's price for those making a down payment of at least 3%.

name: California Proposition 45
title: California Expedited Environmental Review Process for Certain Projects Initiative
description: Make changes to the California Environmental Quality Act to establish deadlines for public agencies to complete environmental review and take required actions for projects deemed essential under the law, limit public agencies' existing requirement to consider a range of project alternatives to reduce environmental impacts, and change the court review process for project approvals by setting deadlines for filing and resolving lawsuits and limiting the evidence and relief the court can consider and order.

name: California Proposition 1
title: California Veteran and Housing Assistance Programs Bond Measure
description: Issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund Multifamily Housing Program, CalVet Home Loan Program, and youth housing.

name: California Proposition 41
title: California Prohibit Excluding New State Taxes from Spending Limit and Require Special Tax Audits Initiative
description: Require pre-election audits for ballot initiatives proposing special taxes once they report collecting 25% of signatures to be included in the voter information pamphlet if it qualifies for the ballot; require state laws or ballot initiatives levying a new special tax enacted after January 1, 2026, to undergo state audits every four years to determine program effectiveness and cost-saving measures; and prohibit the state from enforcing any tax that is exempted or excluded from the state spending limit enacted or effective on or after January 1, 2026.

name: California Proposition 39
title: California Voter Identification and Voter List Maintenance Requirements Initiative
description: Require voters to designate a government-issued ID when registering to vote, and to present that ID for in-person voting or provide the last four digits for mail-in ballots; require election officials to "maintain accurate voter registration lists [and]... use best efforts to verify citizenship attestations using government data" and to report each year the percentage of each county's voter rolls that have been citizenship-verified; require the State Auditor to audit government compliance with these requirements during odd-numbered years and report "findings and recommendations for improving the integrity of elections to the public."

name: California Proposition 38
title: California Establish Immunology and Immunotherapy Research Institute Initiative
description: Authorize the state to issue $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds to fund immunology and immunotherapy research; establish an Immunology and Immunotherapy Research Institute affiliated with the University of California; and award grants to California-based public and nonprofit medical research institutions for immunology and immunotherapy research.

name: California Proposition 2
title: California Budget Stabilization Account Cap Increase and Gann Limit Changes Amendment
description: Increase the Budget Stabilization Account (BSA) cap from 10% of general fund revenue to 20% and excluding deposits into the BSA from the Gann Limit.

name: California Proposition 4
title: California Allow Public Financing of Election Campaigns Measure
description: Repeal the 1988 ban on public financing of campaigns and allow for state and local governments to create programs that provide candidates with public funds under spending limits and eligibility rules.

name: California Proposition 40
title: California One-Time Wealth Tax for State-Funded Healthcare, Education, and Food Assistance Programs Initiative
description: Levy a one-time 5% tax on the accumulated wealth, including shares of capital stock, bonds or other evidences of indebtedness, and any legal or equitable interest, of billionaires in the state to fund state-funded health care programs, such as Medi-Cal, and state food assistance and public education.

name: California Supreme Court Associate Justice Seat 4 - Kelli M. Evans Retention
California Proposition 44
title: California Spending Requirements for Federally Qualified Health Centers Initiative
description: Require nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and FQHC Look-Alikes to spend at least 90% of their annual total revenue on expenses that advance the health center's mission.

name: California Proposition 5
title: California Eliminate State Officer Recall Successor Elections Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to eliminate the election of a successor when a state officer is recalled, thereby leaving the office vacant until it is filled according to state law; allowing for the recalled officer to run again for the same office at the special election, if one is held; and authorize the lieutenant governor to fill the gubernatorial vacancy until the expired term, unless the vacancy occurred before the close of the nomination period for the next statewide election during the first two years of the governor's term, in which a special election would be called and which the winner would serve the remainder of the term.

name: California Proposition 3
title: California Renew State Income Tax Increase for Education Funding Initiative
description: Amend the state constitution to indefinitely extend the top marginal tax rates set to expire in 2031 on single filers earning at least $361,000 or joint filers earning at least $721,000, with 89% of revenue allocated to K–12 schools and 11% to community colleges.

name: Colorado Amendment 85
title: Colorado Require Plain Language and Eighth-Grade Reading Level for Ballot Measures Initiative
description: Amend the Colorado Constitution to require ballot questions to be in plain language at no more than an eighth-grade reading level; and prohibit any state statute from mandating language preceding, following, or in a ballot title of a measure that is not in plain language or exceeds an eighth-grade reading level.

name: Colorado Amendment 84
title: Colorado Require Voter Identification Number for Mail-In Ballots Initiative
description: Amend the Colorado Constitution to require voters casting ballots by mail to provide both their signatures and an identification number, with acceptable forms of identification including the last four digits of their Social Security number, a Colorado REAL ID number, a Colorado REAL ID driver's license number, or the last four digits of another Colorado identification number meeting federal REAL ID requirements.

name: Colorado Court of Appeals - Karl L. Schock Retention
Colorado Court of Appeals - Pax Moultrie Retention
Colorado Amendment 86
title: Colorado Require Commission and Supreme Court Approval for Mid-Decade Congressional Redistricting Initiative
description: Amend the Colorado Constitution to require any mid-decade redistricting plan to be approved by both the state's independent redistricting commission and the Colorado Supreme Court, and prohibit the approval of maps that have been "drawn purposefully to favor one political party."

name: Colorado Supreme Court - William W. Hood, III Retention
title: Colorado Require Commission and Supreme Court Approval for Mid-Decade Congressional Redistricting Initiative
description: Amend the Colorado Constitution to require any mid-decade redistricting plan to be approved by both the state's independent redistricting commission and the Colorado Supreme Court, and prohibit the approval of maps that have been "drawn purposefully to favor one political party."

name: Colorado Amendment 83
title: Colorado Right to Hunt and Fish Initiative
description: Amend Colorado Constitution to provide right to hunt, fish, harvest, and to do so by use of "traditional methods" [undefined"]; to establish hunting and fishing as the "preferred means" [undefined] of managing fish and wildlife populations; to continue the state's authority to regulate hunting, fishing, wildlife management if "necessary" [undefined] for "sound scientific" [undefined] wildlife conservation and management, etc.

name: Colorado Amendment 82
title: Colorado Right to Purchase and Sell Natural Gas for Cooking or Heating in Homes and Businesses Amendment
description: Amend the Colorado Constitution to grant consumers the right to purchase natural gas for cooking or heating in homes or businesses, and for distributors and utilities to sell natural gas to consumers.

name: Colorado Amendment 81
title: Colorado Notification of U.S. Department of Homeland Security for Certain Criminal Charges and Immigration Status Initiative
description: Amend the Colorado Constitution to require state and local law enforcement to notify the U.S. Department of Homeland Security after charging an individual when the individual is not lawfully present in the United States, or if their immigration status cannot be determined after a reasonable effort by law enforcement; and either the individual is charged with a crime of violence, as defined by law, or the individual has been convicted of a prior felony.

Florida Amendment 2 - Exemption of Tangible Personal Property on Agricultural Land from Taxation
title: Florida Exempt Tangible Personal Property Used for Agriculture or Agritourism from Property Taxes Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to exempt tangible personal property, such as farm equipment or tools, from property taxes if the property is typically present on agricultural land, used for farming or agritourism activities, and owned by the landowner or leaseholder of the land.

name: Florida Amendment 3 - Increased Homestead Exemption; Lower Cap on Increases in Non-Homestead Property Assessments
title: Homestead Tax Exemptions, Property Assessments, and Spending Restrictions Amendment
description: Increase the homestead tax exemption for non-school taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, with the amount indexed to inflation starting in 2029; provide that new residents receive a smaller exemption until they've lived in the state for five years; decrease the cap on how much the assessed value of non-homestead properties, such as rentals and commercial buildings, can increase each year from 10% to 5%, except for school district taxes; limit how counties and municipalities can spend property tax revenue on public safety, education, infrastructure, natural resource projects and flood control, local bonds, employee retirement benefits, and government operations; and other changes.

name: Florida Amendment 1 - Budget Stabilization Fund
title: Florida Changes to Budget Stabilization Fund Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to increase the amount of funds that may be retained in the budget stabilization fund from 10% to 25% of net general revenue, require an annual transfer to the fund equal to $750 million or 25% of the general revenue collections (whichever is lesser), and allow for the legislature to suspend the transfer under certain conditions.

name: Hawaii Ballot Measure 1 - Increase Time for Senate to Act on Judicial Appointments Amendment
title: Hawaii Increase Time for Senate to Act on Judicial Appointments Amendment
description: Increase the timeframe for the state senate to consider and act on appointments of judges and justices from 30 days to 60 days for appointments made between April 1 and December 31 when the senate is not in regular session or is soon to adjourn the regular session.

name: Iowa Constitutional Amendment 1
title: Two-Thirds Legislative Vote Requirement for Income Tax Increase Bills Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to require a two-thirds vote of both chambers of the state legislature to pass a bill that would increase the individual or corporate income tax rate or create a new income tax.

name: Idaho Proposition 1: Reproductive Freedom & Privacy Act
title: Idaho Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act Initiative
description: Create a right to reproductive freedom and privacy, declaring that the state can regulate abortion after the point of fetal viability, except in cases of medical emergency, and stating that the government can not interfere with the following personal decisions about reproductive healthcare regarding childbirth care, contraception, fertility treatment, miscarriage care, and prenatal, pregnancy, and postpartum care.

name: Idaho Constitutional Amendment: House Joint Resolution 4
Idaho Constitutional Amendment: House Joint Resolution 6
Indiana Public Question 1 - Bail Amendment
title: Bailable Offenses and Substantial Risk Standard Amendment
description: Amend the Indiana Constitution to provide that offenses, other than murder or treason, are bailable "unless the accused poses a substantial risk to any other person or the community" if the presumption is strong and the state proves that no condition of release will protect the community.

name: Indiana Public Question 2 - City and Town Court Judge Residency Amendment
title: Indiana Residency Requirements for City and Town Court Judges Amendment
description: Requires city and town court judges to reside in either the county where the court is located or the bordering county closest to the court.

name: Louisiana Amendment 4
title: Gubernatorial Two-Term Lifetime Limit Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to provide for a lifetime term limit for the governor, with a maximum of two terms.

name: Massachusetts Question 8 - Eliminate Recreational Marijuana Sales
title: Eliminate Recreational Marijuana Sales and Allow Limited Possession Initiative
description: Make the possession of up to two ounces of marijuana for people aged under 21 a civil offense, and repeal laws that allow the sale, regulation, and taxation of recreational marijuana, laws permitting the personal cultivation of cannabis in homes, alongside laws permitting the possession of up to one ounce of marijuana without penalties, and possession of up to two ounces of marijuana with civil penalties for people aged 21 or older.

name: Massachusetts Question 6 - Nature for All Fund
title: Establish the Nature for All Fund Initiative
description: Create a fund for state money, titled the Nature for All Fund, to be used to fund nature conservation efforts, and require, that before July 1, 2028, 50% of the tax revenue from the sale and use of sporting goods, recreational vehicles, and golf courses be placed in the fund; and that after July 1, 2028, 100% of such tax revenue be placed in the fund.

name: Massachusetts Question 1 - Public Records Law for Legislature and Governor's Office
title: Public Records Requirements for Legislature and Governor’s Office Initiative
description: Make records held by the state legislature and the governor's office subject to the state's public records law, with the exceptions of documents related to the development of policy positions of legislators or the governor and communications between a legislator's office and their constituents concerning a constituent's access to government services.

name: Massachusetts Question 7 - Limit on Required Lot Size for Single-Family Homes
title: Limit on Required Lot Size for Single-Family Homes Initiative
description: Require that cities and towns allow single-family homes on residentially zoned lots that meet minimum standards of at least 5,000 square feet in area, at least 50 feet of frontage on a street or public way, and access to public sewer and water services.

name: Massachusetts Question 9 - Firearm Regulations Referendum
title: Firearm Regulations Referendum
description: Uphold House Bill 4885, which enacted several changes to the state's firearm regulations including: developing an electronic tracking system; prohibiting assault-style firearms (as defined in law); requiring safety certificates to obtain firearm permits; mandating serial numbers for firearms; allowing school administrators and licensed healthcare providers to request that a court issue an Extreme Risk Protection Order; and permitting courts to order firearm surrender when issuing Harassment Prevention Orders.

name: Massachusetts Question 4 - Same-Day Voter Registration
title: Permit Same-Day Voter Registration Initiative
description: Permit same-day voter registration.

name: Massachusetts Question 2 - Collective Bargaining for Public Counsel Services Employees
title: Permit Collective Bargaining for Committee for Public Counsel Services Employees Initiative
description: Permit employees of the Committee for Public Counsel Services (CPCS) to participate in collective bargaining practices, and require the CPCS to request funding from the governor for agreements within 30 days after entering into a collective bargaining contract.

name: Massachusetts Question 3 - Top-Two Primary Elections
title: Top-Two Primary Elections Initiative
description: Create a single primary election in which all candidates would be listed on the same ballot for state elections, regardless of their political affiliation, with the two candidates that receive the most votes would advance to the general election.

name: Massachusetts Question 5 - Change State Tax Revenue Limit
title: Change State Tax Revenue Limit Initiative
description: Change the method of calculating the state's tax revenue limit so that it is equal to the sum of the net amount of state revenue from the year prior and the average growth of wages and salaries in Massachusetts over the past three years, and add income tax revenue collected under Section 2BBBBBB of Chapter 29 of Massachusetts law to the state's definition of state tax revenue.

name: Maryland Question 1 - Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026
title: Maryland Changes to Collective Bargaining for State Employees Amendment
description: Require the governor's budget to provide for expenditures for wages, hours, benefits, and other terms and conditions of employment, provided by a memorandum of understanding covering state employees, and provide for the statutory changes to collective bargaining for state employees, including requiring the selection of a neutral arbitrator and establishing a binding arbitration process.

name: Maryland Appellate Court At Large - Judge Dan Friedman Retention
Maryland Question 2 - Temporary Appointments on the Commission on Judicial Disabilities
title: Maryland Commission on Judicial Disabilities Vacancies Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to authorize the chair of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities to appoint former members to temporarily fill vacancies or allow for the governor to appoint a substitute member or extend the term of an existing member.

name: Maryland Supreme Court Appellate Circuit 4 - Justice Peter Killough Retention
title: Maryland Provide That Nothing in State Constitution Establishes Criteria for Congressional Redistricting Amendment
description: Amend the Maryland Constitution concerning congressional redistricting to provide that constitutional requirements for contiguity, compactness, substantially equal population, and consideration of natural and political subdivision boundaries apply only to state legislative districts, not congressional districts; to allow the General Assembly to grant the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction over challenges to congressional redistricting plans; and provide that the Maryland Constitution establishes no criteria for congressional district boundaries.

name: Maryland Question 3 - Electoral Districts - General Assembly and Congressional Representatives
title: Maryland Provide That Nothing in State Constitution Establishes Criteria for Congressional Redistricting Amendment
description: Amend the Maryland Constitution concerning congressional redistricting to provide that constitutional requirements for contiguity, compactness, substantially equal population, and consideration of natural and political subdivision boundaries apply only to state legislative districts, not congressional districts; to allow the General Assembly to grant the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction over challenges to congressional redistricting plans; and provide that the Maryland Constitution establishes no criteria for congressional district boundaries.

name: Michigan Proposal 1
title: Constitutional Convention Question
description: Hold a state Constitutional Convention.

name: Michigan Proposal 2
title: Michigan Proposal 2
description: Prohibit regulated electric and gas companies, and closely connected individuals, from making campaign contributions to individuals running or holding government offices that would impact them.

name: Missouri Amendment 3
title: Prohibit Abortion and Gender Transition Procedures for Minors Amendment
description: Repeal Amendment 3, which enshrined abortion as a constitutional right up to fetal viability, and prohibit abortion, except in cases of medical emergency, fetal anomaly, rape, or incest, with cases of rape and incest only able to have an abortion performed before 12 weeks; Require parental consent for a minor seeking an abortion, except in cases of medical emergency where consent cannot be obtained; Prohibit fetal organ harvesting after an abortion - defined as the collection of fetal tissue, organs, or fluids for the purpose of selling or collecting for scientific purposes - except for paternity testing, determination of anomaly or condition of the unborn child, or for law enforcement purposes; Provide that women can access healthcare in cases of miscarriages and ectopic pregnancies; Provide for the general assembly to enact laws and regulations regarding the provision of abortions, abortion facilities, and abortion providers; and prohibit gender transition surgeries for minors under eighteen, and prohibit the prescribing of cross-sex hormones or puberty blocking drugs to minors under eighteen for the purposes of gender transition.

name: Missouri Amendment 8
title: Require Election of County Sheriffs Amendment
description: Require the election of county sheriffs in most counties, establishing sheriffs as the chief law enforcement officers in those counties, and limiting the removal of sheriffs from office.

name: Missouri Amendment 7
title: State Investment Fund Amendment
description: Create a permanent public endowment fund managed by the state to generate revenue, and using the earnings to eliminate state-imposed taxes when sufficient to replace them.

name: Missouri Proposition A
title: Missouri Congressional Map Referendum
description: Uphold House Bill 1, which provided for new congressional districts.

name: Montana Initiative 194
title: Exclude Political Spending from Artificial Persons’ Charter Powers Initiative
description: Prohibit artificial persons, including nonprofits, trusts, partnerships, corporations, trade associations, or unincorporated associations, and all entities doing business in Montana, from contributing to campaigns, ballot measure elections, or political parties.

name: Montana Constitutional Initiative 132
title: Require Nonpartisan Judicial Elections Initiative
description: Amend the state constitution to provide that judicial elections remain nonpartisan.

name: North Dakota Constitutional Measure 1
title: 60% Vote Requirement for Constitutional Amendments Measure
description: Requires citizen initiated or legislatively referred constitutional amendments to receive a 60% vote to be adopted.

name: New Hampshire Question 1 - Eliminate the Office of Register of Probate Amendment
title: New Hampshire Abolish Office of Register of Probate Amendment
description: Eliminate the register of probate offices and references to it within the New Hampshire Constitution.

Nevada Question 7
title: Require Voter Identification Initiative
description: Amend the state constitution to require that Nevada residents present a form of photo identification to verify their identity while voting in person, or to verify their identity using the last four digits of their driver's license or Social Security number when voting by mail.

name: Nevada Question 6
title: Right to Abortion Initiative
description: Reaffirm Question 6, which would amend the state constitution to provide for a state constitutional right to an abortion, and for the state to regulate abortion after fetal viability, except where medically indicated to "protect the life or health of the pregnant patient".

name: Ohio State Issue 3 To require voters to present photo identification in order to vote
title: Require Voter Identification Amendment
description: Amend the Ohio constitution to require a photo ID to vote.

name: Oklahoma State Question 847
title: Reduce Annual Increases in Property Values for Tax Calculations Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to change the calculation of the fair cash value of property starting in tax year 2027 by: reducing the annual growth limit of the calculated fair cash value of property from 5% to 4%; reducing the annual growth limit of the calculated fair cash value of property that qualifies for a homestead exemption from 3% to 1.75%; and repealing the prohibition on any increase in fair cash value of homestead property for those aged sixty-five or older whose income exceeds the median amount determined by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

name: Oklahoma State Question 845
title: Changes to Judicial Nominating Commission Amendment
description: Amend the state constitution to mandate the Judicial Nominating Commission require all appointments be made according to congressional districts at the time of the appointment, allow for commissioners to serve two consecutive six-year terms, and remove the provision limiting the commission from having more than three members from one political party.

name: Rhode Island Question 5: Green Economy Bonds - $55,000,000
Rhode Island Question 1: Higher Education Facilities - $275,000,000
title: Rhode Island Higher Education Bond Measure
description: Issue $275 million in bonds to fund the construction and improvement of higher education facilities, including $165 million in bonds to fund the construction of a new integrated health building for the University of Rhode Island, $60 million in bonds to fund the construction of a workforce innovation center at the Community College of Rhode Island, Warwick campus, and $50 million in bonds to fund the construction of a student success and career readiness center at Rhode Island College.

name: Rhode Island Question 2: Housing and Homeownership - $120,000,000
Rhode Island Question 3: Economic Development - $100,000,000
title: Rhode Island Economic and Infrastructure Development Bond Measure
description: Issue $100 million in bonds to fund infrastructure and economic development projects, including $55 million in bonds to fund site development and infrastructure improvements and $45 million in bonds to fund infrastructure improvements to support the state's oceans.

name: South Dakota Amendment L
title: 60% Vote Requirement for Constitutional Amendments Measure
description: Require constitutional amendments to be approved by 60% of voters.

name: South Dakota Amendment I
title: Medicaid Expansion Conditioned on 90% Federal Funding Amendment

name: South Dakota Amendment J

name: South Dakota Amendment K

description: Amend the state constitution to establish a trust fund for unclaimed property.

Wisconsin Question 2 - Prohibit Closing Places of Worship During Emergencies
title: Wisconsin Prohibit Government Closure of Places of Worship During Emergencies Amendment
description: Prohibit the state or any political subdivision from ordering the closure of or forbidding gatherings in places of worship in response to a state of emergency, including public health emergencies.

name: Wisconsin Question 3 - Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment
title: Wisconsin Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment Amendment
description: Prohibit any governmental entity from discriminating or granting preferential treatment based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, public education, public contracting, or public administration.

name: Wisconsin Question 1 - Prohibit Partial Veto to Create or Increase Taxes or Fees
title: Wisconsin Prohibit Partial Veto to Increase Tax or Fee Amendment
description: Amend the Wisconsin Constitution to prohibit the governor from using the partial veto to create or increase any tax or fee.

name: Wyoming Proposition 1 - Homeowner Primary Residence Property Tax Exemption
title: Wyoming Homeowner's Primary Residence Property Tax Exemption Initiative
description: Allows eligible homeowners to exempt 50% of their primary residence's assessed value from property taxes.
